To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the oyster protein hydrolysate prepared by two step hydrolysate of cross linked oyster proteins by microbial transglutinase using Protamex (subtilisin) and Neutrase (alkaline protease) has a potent inhibitory activity against ACE and that five peptides were identified as the active components.

cross-linked oyster proteins hydrolyzed with two step enzymatic hydrolysis using Protamex followed by Neutrase exhibited potent ACE inhibitory activity, and five ACE inhibitory peptides with IC50 values of 16.7 to 93.9 μM were identified from the hydrolysate.
the oyster protein hydrolysate with low IC50 value was obtained by two-step hydrolysis of crosslinked oyster protein with Protamex and neutrase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new ACE inhibitor from oyster proteins.
the development of novel ACE inhibitory peptide from cross-linked oyster protein hydrolysates using a combination of six different proteases and the subsequent purification of five peptides.
the development of an antihypertension nutraceutical derived from oyster protein, and its application as a food ingredient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work is the first to describe the use of microbial transglutamination in the production of an ACE inhibitory peptide from oyster.

the oyster protein cross linked by microbial transglutinase and hydrolyzed by the combined use of Protamex and neutrase exhibited a potent antihypertension effect in SHR, and that the antihypertention effect of the oyste protein hydrolysate was due to the five purified ACE inhibitory peptides.
this research has demonstrated the potential for the use of oysters as a source of nutraceuticals for the management of hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cross linked oysters proteins were successfully used to produce ACE inhibitory peptide with potent antihypertension activity.
we have successfully developed an ACE inhibitory peptide from oyster proteins.
cross linking by microbial transtglutaminase is an effective method for improving ACE inhibitory activities of oyster protein hydrolysates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oyster proteins can be a good source of ACE inhibitory peptides.
oyster hydrolysates are a potential source of antihypertensives.
the oyster protein can be used as a source of bioactive peptides with ACE inhibitory activity and antihypertension effects.
